title: Provide governed current-main synchronization for active Work Items
rawUserRequest: Continue executing the authorized remediation plan to completion; when a workflow problem is discovered, create a corrective Work Item rather than applying a temporary workaround.

declaredIntent.summary: Correct the missing governed synchronization boundary exposed by #663 without permitting a manual lifecycle bypass.

outOfScope: Manual Git rebase, merge, force-push, provider mutation, archive rewrite, or branch deletion by a caller outside the synchronization command
Changing #663 implementation or provider state before its synchronization evidence is valid
Weakening predecessor, Start Receipt, ancestry, clean-worktree, or scope validation

sources.reason: The existing resume path validates an already rebased branch and a completed predecessor but cannot establish a legal current-main transition for an interrupted active Work Item.
Defines immutable receipt and resume-lineage validation that the new transition must preserve.
Canonical lifecycle documentation currently describes rebase before the validator and must reflect any supported command boundary.
Provider finding and acceptance created from #663 supported-resume fail-closed evidence.

riskAssessment.reason: Synchronizing an active Work Item to a newer default base can invalidate scope, verification, and predecessor lineage unless the transition is atomic, source-bound, and fail closed.

reasons: The user authorized automatic remediation; this changes lifecycle, Git evidence, installed templates, and documentation.

override.approvalEvidence: The user granted standing authorization for required Work Item corrections, lifecycle completion, and provider operations in this thread.
override.reason: Strict lifecycle and evidence-integrity verification without a release operation.
notRunChecks: Release-preflight and distribution verification are inapplicable because this Work Item neither changes release-owned resources nor publishes.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly authorized automatic corrective Work Items; #663 supplied a reproducible supported-command failure and no unsafe workaround will be used.

preReviewWarnings: Review source binding, ancestry, dirty-state rejection, predecessor semantics, and template/installed-runtime parity.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Lifecycle and Git-history changes require immutable before-edit and before-finish checkpoints.

acceptance: `make ai-synchronize-work-item CONTRACT=<active-contract> BASE_REMOTE=<remote> BASE_BRANCH=<default>` performs an eligible local dedicated-branch rebase onto the exact remote default target and then atomically records old/new base, branch/worktree identity, Contract/Summary digests, and append-only transition evidence.

Before any rebase, the command rejects dirty, archived, detached/base branch, foreign Work Item, stale remote, non-ancestor, provider-mutated, unrelated, or already-synchronized states; it never pushes, force-pushes, opens a PR, mutates provider state, changes immutable Start Receipt, or rewrites archive evidence.

A rebase conflict is aborted automatically and leaves the active Contract/Summary and recorded lifecycle evidence byte-identical; a successful rebase invalidates prior verification and requires fresh preflight plus current-generation checks before Finish.
Regression tests cover an allowed real Git synchronization, automatic conflict abort, repeated invocation, stale predecessor/evidence, and every pre-rebase rejection boundary.

`docs/reference/ai-cockpit-work-item-lifecycle.md`, `.ai/cockpit/README.md`, and installed-template counterparts document the exact command, authority limits, recovery conditions, and parity; the generated capability matrix is refreshed by its canonical generator.
guidelines: Keep the command narrower than Git rebase: it may establish only a verified baseline transition and must never mutate Git refs or provider state.
Preserve immutable Start Receipt and archive facts; use append-only, digest-bound transition evidence.
Maintain source-template-installed runtime parity for all public lifecycle commands.
New public APIs and recovery limits must be documented in canonical lifecycle guidance.

intent.problem: #663 is a valid active Work Item created from an older main. The existing resume writer correctly rejects it because it is not already rebased and lacks a closed predecessor; however, the lifecycle offers no governed way to create a legal synchronization transition. A manual rebase would leave no authoritative evidence and violates the no-workaround rule.
constraints: The command may perform only a local controlled rebase after all fail-closed checks; provider and remote Git mutations remain outside its authority.
Dedicated Work Item identity, clean state, remote/default target, ancestry, and Contract/Summary/Start Receipt integrity are required before an active evidence write.
Baseline transition invalidates prior verification and requires fresh preflight plus current-generation checks; it never makes Finish eligible.
Source and installed template expose equivalent runtime and documentation behavior.
intent.rationale: A narrow, receipt-bound command makes the necessary local Git rebase explicit, repeatable, and auditable rather than requiring an undocumented manual lifecycle bypass; provider and publication controls remain unchanged.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An eligible clean active Work Item is behind origin/main and has a valid synchronization authority record.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The command locally rebases the dedicated branch and writes one digest-bound active transition receipt without provider, remote, archive, or immutable Start Receipt mutation.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use a temporary Git fixture to prove the branch has the target ancestor after rebase, compare provider/immutable file bytes before/after, then validate the recorded transition.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The active Work Item has a dirty worktree, detached/base branch, stale remote target, foreign identity, or non-ancestor history.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The command rejects without writing active evidence or mutating Git/provider state.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Exercise each invalid fixture and assert error plus byte-for-byte no-write postconditions.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A caller repeats a transition or attempts to use stale or forged predecessor, receipt, Contract, or Summary evidence.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The command rejects replay and evidence inconsistency fail closed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add direct writer and CLI fixtures for replay and each stale or mismatched evidence input.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A source repository and installed template expose the synchronization command and recovery documentation.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Parity tests prove equivalent command availability and documented authority limits.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run installed-runtime parity tests plus documentation and capability-truth generation checks.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user authorized automatic execution and requires workflow defects to be corrected through Work Items rather than temporary patches.

rollbackNote: Revert the synchronization command, schema/validation changes, template distribution, documentation, and tests together; no Git/provider mutation is performed by the command.
